summary: Documented M2-S04 (Case queues and public groups for Tier 1 General, Tier 2 Engineering and Billing) after step-tester marked it tested. Re-rendered PLAN.md; appended six decisions (D-M2S04-01..06) plus four planner open items (O-M2S04-01..04) to decisions.md; wrote six new workbook rows to a new Section 6 file (workbook/06-automation.md, CWB-AUT-001..006 for the three Queue and three Group components) and three new rows to Other Configuration (CWB-OTHER-010..012 for package.xml, deploy-order.md and queue-retirement-runbook.md); minted five new requirement ids (REQ-021..025) and wrote their traceability.md rows, linking Q26/Q29/Q30/Q88/Q89 and the corresponding requirement.md lines to the six artefacts and the step's checker plus four manual tests; staged a four-case UAT draft plus a five-criterion acceptance-criteria file in the session scratchpad and linted both clean. Set the step's status to documented via build_plan.py. The workbook placement diverges from a literal reading of Step 4's type map (access -> Sections 3/4) because Queue/Group content fits neither; Section 6 (Automation) was chosen instead, grounded in build-orchestration.md's own routing row and the configuration-workbook-authoring skill's own CWB-AUT- precedent, and recorded as D-M2S04-06 for a human to confirm at the gate.
confidence_rationale: Per Step 11's override: every artefact produced a workbook row, every row carries a real source_req_id, and every requirement this step serves has a traceability row with no duplicates on re-render. MEDIUM rather than HIGH because two conditions in the MEDIUM row apply: an artefact (Queue/Group) could not be placed in a Step-4-mapped section without judgment (resolved as D-M2S04-06, Section 6), and two requirement ids (REQ-022, REQ-023) had their source clarification inferred from requirement.md text plus a related-but-not-identical clarification id (Q29, Q13) rather than read off a single unambiguous field on the step. Not LOW: no row was written with an empty source_req_id or an empty verification cell, and the step's test results were fully readable.

inputs_received.concurrency_note: M2-S03 is being reset/rebuilt in a concurrent session per this run's own instructions; only M2-S04 rows were written and only this run's appended decisions.md entries were added -- no M2-S03 row was touched, consistent with the three Profile: orphans check_rtm.py reports at build scope, which belong to that other session's step.

dimensions_skipped.reason: The step's declared type (access) maps to Sections 3/4 in Step 4's table, and neither fits a Queue or Group artefact. Resolved by content-based judgment (D-M2S04-06) rather than a mechanical lookup, because Step 4's table itself does not offer an access-vs-content override clause.
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Add an explicit content-based override clause to agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 4's mapping table so a future run does not need a per-run judgment call recorded in decisions.md.

process_observations.observation: M2-S04 is the first metadata-builder step in this build whose package.xml, deploy-order.md and markdown runbook were all three declared in outputs[] from the point check-outputs first ran, closing the undeclared-deploy-order.md pattern decisions.md records as still open on M1-S01, M1-S02 and M2-S02 (O-M1S01-01-adjacent, O-M1S02-02, O-M2S02-01).

The data-skew checker's exit-1 gap the metadata-builder envelope recorded as an open checker limitation was closed the same day by a library fix (commit d7cc43e04) found by this very build -- re-running the identical declared-adjacent command over these artefacts in this documentation pass now exits 0 with three accurately-reworded WARNs instead of a false 'unused' framing.

Five REQ-021..025 traceability rows had to route their status mostly to 'In Build' rather than 'In UAT' because six downstream steps (M3-S03, M3-S04, M3-S05, M4-S04, M5-S01, M2-S05) all depend on this one -- more fan-out than any prior documented step in this build, which makes M2-S04 a single point where a re-plan of any one of those six steps has wide traceability-row consequences.

Two independent documented gaps on this step both trace to the same missing answer (Tier 2's shared-mailbox address is a posture, not a value): the checker-description WARN-count mismatch (O-M2S04-01) and the manual-test criterion/artefact mismatch (O-M2S04-02). One clarification answer would close both simultaneously, which is worth surfacing before a re-plan treats them as two separate fixes.

This step's declared type (access) disagrees with standards/build-orchestration.md's own step-type table, which files Queue metadata under routing -- the same tension metadata-builder's own envelope flagged unresolved. This run resolved only the workbook-section consequence (D-M2S04-06); the plan's step-type field itself is unchanged and the underlying disagreement is unresolved at the plan level.
M2-S04 is now documented, and its deploy-order.md and package.xml are ready inputs for milestone-level cross-step checks once the remaining M2 steps (M2-S03, M2-S05) are documented.
process_observations.followup_reason: Because milestone-verifier runs cross-step checks and the acceptance report only once every M2 step is documented, and this run leaves M2-S03 as the remaining gap (in a concurrent session) and M2-S05 as pending.
